chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Muhammad al-Wasiti who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

"Do not leave [omitting] after every prayer - I seek refuge for myself and what my Lord has granted me in [the name of] Allah the One, the Eternal - until you conclude it, and I seek refuge for myself and what my Lord has granted me in 'The Lord of the Fajr' until you conclude it, and I seek refuge for myself and what my Lord has granted me in 'The Lord of Mankind' until you conclude it."

key_terms.رَبِّ الْفَلَقِ: The Lord of the Fajr (Surah Al-Falaq)

ai.seo_question: What supplications should be recited after every prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes reciting the Mu'awwidhatayn (Surahs Al-Falaq and An-Nas) along with specific invocations of Allah's oneness and sufficiency after every prayer, a practice rooted in the Shia tradition of seeking refuge from evil immediately following worship. This emphasis on post-prayer supplication highlights the spiritual vulnerability of the believer and the necessity of divine protection in daily life. The inclusion of 'Al-Samad' (The Eternal Refuge) underscores the reliance on Allah's self-sufficiency for safeguarding the soul.
